failures.criterion: Filter drift (spec), and the review's round-1 finding that the check must hold the tags a claimed go command compiles with: GOFLAGS carries -tags too, and the check reads it nowhere
failures.evidence: line_command (ci_filter_coverage.py:368-412) reads -tags only from flags after `go <subcommand>`. A `GOFLAGS=-tags=…` in front of the command (shlex gives it as a word before `go`, which is skipped) or in the step's or job's env is never read. The go command reads GOFLAGS and applies its -tags whenever the line passes none. I checked this outside the check: in a module whose cmd/app has a `//go:build probe` test importing ./other, `GOFLAGS=-tags=probe go list -deps -test ./cmd/app` lists example.com/m/other, and without it 0 lines match. Red tests, commit 0f243125 on legion/INFRA-520, in .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh: the case 'GOFLAGS set in front of a claimed go command compiles a file outside the job's filter' (`run: GOFLAGS=-tags=probe go test ./cmd/app ./lib`) and the case 'GOFLAGS in a claimed go command's step env compiles a file outside the job's filter' (step `env: GOFLAGS: -tags=probe`). Each adds mod/cmd/app/probe_test.go (//go:build probe, imports example.com/m/other) and expects exit 1 and output naming other. Command: `PATH=<python with PyYAML>:$PATH bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh` -> 'Results: 48 passed, 4 failed' (both fixtures exit 0 today). No ci.yaml job sets GOFLAGS today (grep finds none), so nothing is broken on the tree now; the hole is open to the next such edit, exactly as the reviewer's trailing -tags was. Fix that fails closed: treat a GOFLAGS (inline before the go command, or in the step or job env) as part of the line, reading its -tags into the line's tags; or refuse GOFLAGS on a claimed command unless its Run lists it in env.
